clue.text: It may display welcome for person being badly treated

definitions.meaning: the thing by a front door that often has WELCOME printed on it
someone who lets others walk all over them

explanation.surface: A sign of welcome turns out to be for someone who gets trampled on.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads like a shop sign or banner, but it is the literal mat at the front door; the second half is the figurative use.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is a doormat lets everyone walk over them, just as people wipe their feet on the real thing.

clue.text: Working sailor lands on Jupiter moon to establish city

indicators.note: the first pieces come down on top of the next, as a down clue is built from the top

parts.note: on = working, as a machine that is on
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A space sailor touches down on a moon of Jupiter to found a colony.
explanation.walkthrough: Most solvers know Ontario as the Canadian province; the definition is fair because there is also a city of Ontario in California.
explanation.definitionFit: Ontario is a city in southern California, as well as the Canadian province.

clue.text: Lover representing NATO in central Paris

indicators.note: the letter is swapped for its word in the NATO phonetic alphabet
take the letter at the centre of the word

parts.note: R is the middle letter of PARIS
the NATO phonetic alphabet word for R

explanation.surface: Some romantic figure stands in for the military alliance in the heart of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The NATO phonetic alphabet (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie…) gives each letter a code word, and R's is Romeo, which also names Shakespeare's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero became a byword, so a romantic suitor is called by his name.

clue.text: Style of exotic trade supported by business

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged
in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, which holds it up

explanation.surface: A description of the way a foreign trading venture, backed by a firm, is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Style of exotic trade' reads as one phrase about commerce, but 'Style' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A named style in design and architecture, the geometric look of the 1920s and 30s.

clue.text: One who saves initially is against hoarding after disorder

indicators.note: take the first letter of each following word
the first letters come after the piece for disorder

parts.note: first letters of Is Against Hoarding

explanation.surface: A thrifty saver starts squirrelling money away after things get chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One who saves' pulls toward a thrifty person with a piggy bank; the saving here is of souls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Messiah is the promised saviour or deliverer.

clue.text: You register drug to pick up praise?

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words are heard rather than read

explanation.surface: A question about signing in to collect a prescription, oddly ending on praise.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for ecstasy. Said quickly, 'you log E' runs together into eulogy.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech or piece of writing full of praise, often for someone who has died.

clue.text: Providing support by transferring workers temporarily

definitions.meaning: backing a motion in a meeting, the sense said SEC-ond
staff seconded to another post are moved there for a spell

explanation.surface: A manager helps out another team by lending them some staff for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: SEC-onding a motion, but se-CONDING an employee.
explanation.definitionFit: To second is both to back a proposal and to move an employee to another post for a time.

clue.text: It tells broadcaster what to say reporting traffic build-up

definitions.text: It tells broadcaster what to say

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so what follows is heard

explanation.surface: A news presenter reading out the traffic report from a prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter, the screen a presenter reads from.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocue shows the presenter the script to read on air.

clue.text: Rehashed leftovers a hit at this high class establishment

indicators.note: a rehash cooks the ingredients up again in a new form

explanation.surface: A posh hotel's kitchen serves reheated leftovers and the diners love them.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture of rehashed leftovers is ironic: they are the last thing a luxury hotel would admit to serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotels are graded by stars, and five is the top rating, so 'high class establishment' describes it.

clue.text: Something very small splitting Chat Room in half

indicators.note: splitting a word breaks it into two parts, so each of the next two words is cut in the middle
keep one half, here the back half, of each word

explanation.surface: Something tiny breaking up an online chat room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something very small splitting' suggests splitting the atom, a nod to the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiny basic unit of matter.

clue.text: Journey delayed, blocked by idiotic extremists — three times!

definitions.note: triplicate means in three copies; 'three times' is the sense of 'in triplicate'

indicators.note: the piece for delayed is blocked, with something stuck inside it
the extremes, first and last letters, of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of IdiotiC, placed inside LATE to make LA(IC)TE

explanation.surface: An exasperated traveller's train is held up by hotheads, for the third time.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark carries the surface's irritation; the definition is 'three times', as in forms filled out in triplicate. TRIP + LA(IC)TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in triplicate is done three times over.

clue.text: Rhythmic feel is an essential part of vinyl record

definitions.meaning: the swing or feel of a piece of music

definitions.text: an essential part of vinyl record
definitions.meaning: the spiral channel the stylus runs along

explanation.surface: A music fan says rhythm is what makes a vinyl record.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the same music world, so the surface reads as one statement about records.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is both the swing of a rhythm and the track cut into a record.

clue.text: Brussels information is about conservative providing dodgy science

indicators.note: the IS goes about, around, the letter for conservative

parts.note: Brussels is home to the EU institutions
C = Conservative, placed inside IS to make I(C)S

explanation.surface: A news item about the EU briefing a Tory politician on some shaky research.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugenics, the idea of improving humans by selective breeding, is a discredited pseudo-science.

clue.text: Lecture on ancient defensive structure surrounded by hotels

indicators.note: the ancient structure sits inside the hotels

parts.note: Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H; the first of the two hotels
Hotel is the NATO alphabet word for H; the second of the two hotels

explanation.surface: A guide lectures about an old castle ringed by hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotels' is plural so it supplies two H's, one each side. Hotel is H in the NATO alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for talking at length, as if giving a lecture nobody asked for.

clue.text: Conscripts staff for one producing deeds etc.

parts.note: to draft = to conscript, so conscripts = drafts

explanation.surface: An army that conscripts soldiers to fill jobs for a legal clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Both wordplay words are verbs, not the nouns they look like: conscripts means drafts, and staff means man.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftsman drafts documents such as legal deeds.

clue.text: Speaker chooses line that's part of picture

indicators.note: what follows is said out loud by a speaker

explanation.surface: An orator selects a line from a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the standard abbreviation for line, said as its letter name 'el'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is one of the tiny dots that make up a digital picture.

clue.text: Suggest using spare cash for launch?

definitions.meaning: to put an idea forward tentatively
the spare change put in a till at the start of trading, the word also meaning to launch a company

explanation.surface: Someone proposes putting surplus money towards a new product launch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half bundles two more senses: a float is spare change kept in a till, and floating a company launches it on the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: Float means to put forward an idea, as well as a cash float and launching a firm.

clue.text: Hero worshipping youth provides name to boss

indicators.note: one letter is given to the word
it is given into the middle of the word for boss

parts.note: N = name, placed inside the boss word after its third letter

explanation.surface: A young fan of a celebrity gives his name to his manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero worshipping youth' looks like a teenage fan; Hero is the priestess in Greek myth, and Leander the young man who swam the Hellespont nightly to see her.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander was the youth who loved Hero in the Greek legend.

clue.text: Forcibly enlist group of journalists

definitions.meaning: to force someone into service, as navies once seized sailors
journalists are collectively the press, and a group is a gang

explanation.surface: Reporters being rounded up and made to join up.
explanation.walkthrough: Press gangs once seized men to serve in the navy; the second reading splits it into the press (journalists) as a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To press-gang someone is to force them into service.

clue.text: His vote is wasted? No chance

indicators.note: wasted as in drunk and all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A cynical voter asks whether his ballot counts, and is told it has no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark splits the clue: the first part is the wordplay, 'No chance' the curt reply.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Shove it!' is a rude refusal, meaning much the same as 'no chance!'

clue.text: Turning cool over trip that produces nothing

indicators.note: the word for cool is turned round
in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

explanation.surface: A cold spell drawn out over a pointless outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cool' here is a verb, what a fan does. Naff all is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff all is British slang for nothing whatsoever.

clue.text: In the middle, Oscars turned really raunchy

indicators.note: take the middle two letters of each word

explanation.surface: Midway through the Oscars ceremony things got steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like a reversal instruction but is only a word to be cored; the indicator covers all three six-letter words.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal means to do with bodily, sexual desire, so raunchy.

clue.text: Actor sat in disguise of old style singer

indicators.note: the letters are dressed up in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor posing, disguised as a period singer.
explanation.walkthrough: A castrato was a male singer castrated before puberty to keep a high voice, common in 17th and 18th century opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrati were singers of an old, now abandoned, operatic tradition.

clue.text: Unique attitude aristocrat has no time for

indicators.note: T, for time, is removed from both words

explanation.surface: A snob who can't be bothered with a certain kind of manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A toff is British slang for an upper-class person. 'Tone' as in tone of voice gives attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something unique, made or happening only once.

clue.text: Against supporting former partner, a retired criminal

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits below the first, holding it up

parts.note: con = against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone who opposes backing their former spouse, a retired crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in the clue in the reverse of their order in the answer, because CON supports EX from below.
explanation.definitionFit: An ex-con is a former convict, one who has retired from crime.

clue.text: The first gardeners? Some Londoners believe so

definitions.meaning: the first couple in Genesis, placed in the Garden of Eden to tend it

explanation.surface: A question about who first tended a garden, answered by a nod to Londoners' faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, spoken in East London, swaps a word for a rhyming phrase: 'Would you Adam and Eve it?' means 'would you believe it?'
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve were placed in Eden to tend it, so the first gardeners.

clue.text: Check top class beverage from India

parts.note: A1 = top class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a premium drink imported from India.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate, and setters let the digit 1 stand for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is spiced tea, the everyday drink of India.

clue.text: Seafood found around river furrow

indicators.note: the seafood word is found wrapped around the river letter

parts.note: a winkle is a small edible sea snail
R = river, placed inside the seafood after its first letter

explanation.surface: Shellfish discovered along a riverbank channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Winkles are small sea snails sold at British seaside stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrinkle is a crease or furrow, in skin or cloth.

clue.text: Like a warm feeling you get next to fire

parts.note: at = next to, as in 'at the door'
an ingle is a fire in a hearth, as in inglenook

explanation.surface: The cosy glow you feel sitting beside the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is the warmth of sitting by a fireside, which is exactly the tingling glow the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Atingle means tingling, as with a warm glow.
